questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching the intersection with its siren and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or siren, finish crossing. Then move to the right and stop. You must let police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles pass first.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: To turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: A child is about to run into the street. What should you do?

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: If a child or any pedestrian is about to step in front of your car, give a sharp horn blast. This warns them to stay out of the street.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of a two-lane road. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. The driver behind you wants to drive faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane so you don't impede the flow of traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let the other vehicles pass.
Move into the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane to drive slower, enter the road, or turn right.

questions.question: When is the highway most slippery?

options.text: If it has been raining several hours.
If it has just begun to rain.
If it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has just begun to rain.
questions.explanation: The road is most slippery when rain first starts. Rain mixes with dirt and oil on the road, creating a slick film.

questions.question: The MVA will suspend your license if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is:

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.
0.06 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: If you drive in Maryland, you agree to take a blood alcohol test. The MVA will suspend your license if your BAC is 0.08 percent or higher.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back to your original lane only when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough room to safely get back in front of them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The roadway ends ahead.
Drivers must bear either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns you that the road splits. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending. Be ready to change lanes.

questions.question: When driving from an alley or driveway onto a sidewalk to enter traffic, you must:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
questions.explanation: You must stop before entering a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and other traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red traffic light, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, make sure the way is clear, then go.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, you should:

options.text: Look toward the center of the roadway.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This prevents the bright lights from blinding you and lets you see enough to stay on course. Do not keep your own bright lights on in response.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green text or symbols. They tell you traffic laws you must follow.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Enter the far-right lane immediately and speed up to match traffic.
Use the road shoulder to speed up to traffic speed.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: Look for a gap in traffic first, then speed up and enter. Wait while stopped if needed until a safe gap appears.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and gently using the brakes.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at the same speed as in dry conditions.
Use your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When driving too fast on wet roads, your tires lose contact with the road and ride on water. This is hydroplaning. Drive slower in rain to prevent it.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: When a school bus picks up or drops off children, you must:

options.text: Stop no matter which direction you are driving.
Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop no matter which direction you are driving.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before you reach a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children. This is true no matter which direction you are driving.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you start to skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Turn your steering wheel in the direction the skid is moving. If your vehicle has anti-lock brakes, press the brakes hard and steer straight.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: Can finish the turn in either of the two lanes.
May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must always stay in the right lane while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks have a bigger difference between these paths. Because of this, trucks often need to swing wide to make a right turn.

questions.question: If you feel your tires have lost contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas pedal and do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires are gripping the road again before you try to stop or turn.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up a little.
Get ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A vehicle could be broken down just out of sight. Slow down as you approach hills and curves so you can stop if you need to.
